column1: # pgrdf.surface() manifest — authored classification of every export.
# Classes: stable (contract; removal/signature change = breaking release)
#          internal (reachable but not API; no compatibility promise)
#          spike (development measurement harness; may vanish without notice)
#          deprecated (superseded; the note names the replacement)
# Notes are CONSUMER-FACING: they describe what the function is and how to
# use it well, in words that stand alone. A completeness test enforces this
# file covers every extension-owned function in both directions.
_path_walk(preds bigint[], graph_id bigint, seed bigint, follow_inverse boolean, max_depth integer, path_id integer, per_graph boolean)
column3: the breadth-first walk behind SPARQL + and * property paths (visited set per start, exact depth truncation, memory budget pgrdf.path_max_pairs); called by translated SQL, not an API. Since 0.6.37
trigger function lock_graph installs on a locked graph's partition: refuses direct SQL INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE with 55P03 and the unlock cure as HINT. Not callable as an API. Since 0.6.37
ensures the quad partition for a raw graph id; consumers create graphs by IRI with add_graph(iri)
binds an explicit id/IRI pair; refuses rebinding either side. Consumers create graphs by IRI

create (or ensure) a graph by IRI; returns its graph_id; idempotent. Ids are never reused (since 0.6.39): the IRI is the identity, the id a handle. Creating a new graph needs SELECT and INSERT on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs (42501 otherwise, HINT names the grant); the partition DDL itself runs as the storage owner. Since 0.6.37
which build of version() this binary is (git describe at compile time); 'unknown' means the build did not supply one. Since 0.6.29
can the current role clear graphs? true when it holds SELECT and DELETE on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads, the exact rule clear_graph enforces. Since 0.6.38

can the current role create graphs? true when it holds SELECT and INSERT on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs, the exact rule add_graph enforces. Read this rather than inferring from table ownership. Since 0.6.37
can the current role drop graphs? true when it holds SELECT and DELETE on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs, the exact rule drop_graph enforces. Since 0.6.37

remove every triple from a graph; the graph itself remains. Refuses on a locked graph (55P03). Needs SELECT and DELETE on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads (42501 otherwise, HINT names the grant); the partition TRUNCATE runs as the storage owner. Since 0.6.38
remove every triple from a graph by IRI; unknown IRI refuses (42704)

create a NEW graph by IRI, or refuse 42710 if the IRI exists; the HINT names the existing graph_id and its recorded source digest, so a caller can reuse it or choose another IRI. Atomic against concurrent claims. Needs SELECT and INSERT on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs. add_graph(iri) stays get-or-create. Since 0.6.37
SPARQL CONSTRUCT; rows are JSONB triples suitable for put_construct_rows
copy src into dst. Caution: appends, and carries inferred triples with it — clear dst first for a clean copy, re-materialize after
copy by IRI; same append-and-carry caution as the id form
total quads (asserted + inferred) in one graph; graph 0 is the default graph
SPARQL DESCRIBE; rows are JSONB triples

drop a graph and its partition; refuses over inferred rows unless cascade (2BP01); cannot drop the default partition. Needs SELECT and DELETE on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs (42501 otherwise); the partition DDL runs as the storage owner. Since 0.6.37
drop by IRI; unknown IRI refuses (42704)
lexical value of a dictionary term id, as returned in query results and inventory

column1: graph_diff(a bigint, b bigint, side text, predicate text, class text)
column3: the triples that differ from graph a to graph b, blank-node-aware: side '-' (only in a) or '+' (only in b), terms in N-Triples form, component NULL for a ground triple else its blank-node component's rdfc-1.0 digest. Ordered side then canonical line, so OFFSET/LIMIT paging is deterministic. predicate/class narrow the comparison; a component is returned whole if any triple matches. Empty iff the graphs are isomorphic. Since 0.6.37

counts of what changed from graph a to graph b, with its method label: ground removed/added/common (triples), components removed/added/common (a multiset of rdfc-1.0 component digests) and their triples, by_predicate (ground + component triples) and by_type (rdf:type triples per class). Since 0.6.37

canonical graph identity, method rdfc-1.0-sha256: survives reload and blank-node relabelling; equal AND unequal are both conclusive. Absent graph refuses (42704); empty graph answers. Not comparable with structural_digest values. Since 0.6.32
graph_id for an IRI, or NULL when unknown — check before feeding into strict functions, which silently pass NULL through
term-position integrity report (non-IRI predicates, literal subjects); unclean graphs validate vacuously and should be reloaded
a graph's asserted triples as canonical N-Triples, byte-sorted, one line per triple; inferred rows never export (they re-derive). Absent graph refuses (42704). Since 0.6.34

every registered graph with IRI, asserted/inferred counts, lock state, materialization freshness (current/stale/never/unknown), source_sha256 and source_loads (what the graph was loaded from; since 0.6.37) and identity_digest (a locked graph's cached rdfc-1.0 digest while lock custody holds; since 0.6.37) — the supported alternative to reading private tables. Since 0.6.34

portable manifest of one graph: three digests each carrying its method (bytes / rdfc-1.0 identity / fd1 structure), counts, engine identity, and what is NOT carried. Pair with export_graph to build a redistributable package. Since 0.6.34
IRI bound to a graph_id, or NULL when unknown

per-call completeness figures (path_depth_truncations, filter_clauses_dropped) for the most recent sparql/construct/describe call in THIS session; session-local, so other sessions cannot pollute it. Read it right after the query. Since 0.6.34
